stories.title: US flights resume after stoppage, further delays expected
stories.summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration has lifted a nationwide grounding of flights after a communications failure at air traffic control centres triggered the longest nationwide shutdown since the 11 September 2001 attacks. More than 6,600 flights were cancelled and 8,600 delayed, with another 1,500 already cancelled for Sunday, according to FlightRadar24. Over 1.5 million passengers were scheduled to depart US airports after 4pm ET (2100 GMT), shortly after the ground stop began, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium. Analysts said the four-hour nationwide grounding could disrupt airline schedules for days. 'Old hardware' was to blame for the US air travel stoppage, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told reporters at a White House press briefing. Mr Duffy said switches and routers had become overloaded with data and went down.

stories.title: How Ireland embraced 'pre-loved' e-commerce
stories.summary: Jeans that are too tight, a leather jacket from years ago, that fabulous wedding guest dress that will never be worn again. A few years ago, the only option for getting rid of unwanted clothes was bringing them to a charity shop, giving away to friends and family or recycle. It's not surprising that Irish shoppers have an urge to get rid of stuff – statistics show we've accumulated a lot of it. An average Irish household spends around €2,000 on clothes and shoes a year, according to the CSO data from 2022-2023 (since then, that figure has likely increased to around €2,500 due to inflation). Ireland stands out among its European peers when it comes to the amount of new textiles – mostly clothes – bought each year. According to the Environmental Protection Agency, Ireland's clothing consumption was 53 kg per capita in 2019, well above the EU average.

stories.title: Ireland look to build on good start as Fiji come to town
stories.summary: Depending on which direction you look, Andy Farrell has either rotated heavily or not rotated enough for this evening's meeting with Fiji at Aviva Stadium. The Ireland head coach has made seven changes to the side that defeated Argentina a week ago. A couple of those players, such as Dan Sheehan and Sean Jansen, miss out due to injury, another few – Joe McCarthy, Hugo Keenan and Robbie Henshaw – are rested, while Craig Casey and Stuart McCloskey swap to the bench and will feature against Fiji this evening. It's certainly nowhere near an experimental selection, with experienced talent like Jamison Gibson-Park, Bundee Aki, Rónan Kelleher, James Ryan and Josh van der Flier among those coming in, and it seems Andy Farrell is using this clash with Fiji to prepare his players for South Africa, rather than to keep them fresh. With just eight games left until the World Cup training camp begins, and Farrell already acknowledging the ground that his team needs to make up if they are to go to Australia as genuine contenders, it's clear the Ireland coach is viewing this Nations Championship window as a crucial launchpad to get this Ireland team flowing. We saw glimpses of it last week, where they looked a far more cohesive unit compared to their summer games in Australia and New Zealand. Their lineout, which had statistically been the worst of the 12 teams in the summer block, was much improved with the return of Ryan Baird, who also caused havoc on Argentina's throw.

stories.title: Nicola Coughlan delivers powerful message on Late Late
stories.summary: Nicola Coughlan told Friday's Late Late Show that she hopes her starring role in the new Channel 4 drama I Am Helen will encourage people in abusive relationships to seek help. Bridgerton and Derry Girls star Coughlan has developed I Am Helen with the award-winning series' writer-creator-director Dominic Savage, who collaborates with his leading actors on the stories for each I Am... season. When Late Late Show host Patrick Kielty said the two-part drama "couldn't be more timely", Coughlan replied: "Unfortunately so." "The I Ams are very unusual projects, if anyone hasn't seen them," she explained. "They're basically completely improvised. So, there's a story there, but you show up on set every day with no script. The fear levels every day of going into work, you're like, 'I can't do it. It's too much'." "This one is about the breakdown of a relationship," she continued.

stories.title: 7 whimsical nail designs to try for the festive season
stories.summary: While many of us may be partaking in the naked nails trend this season, online ‘whimsymaxxing’ has taken the nail world by storm. Distinguished by mismatched patterns, spontaneous colour combinations and elaborate embellishments, the aesthetic is the antithesis of the understated manicures that have dominated the nail trends of late. And with Christmas approaching, there’s arguably no better time to embrace a little excess. From miniature bows and festive characters to shimmering metallics and three-dimensional nail art, the trend encourages experimentation rather than following any particular rules. But according to celebrity nail artist Jenni Draper, who has worked with stars including Adele, Julia Roberts and Rihanna, the idea of having fun with your manicure is hardly new. "I actually think whimsymaxxing is something many nail technicians and their clients have been embracing for a long time," she tells the Press Association.

stories.title: Tánaiste seeks views on Irish unity from party leaders
stories.summary: The Tánaiste Simon Harris has written to all political leaders across the island to seek their views on Irish unity and to explore what common ground exists on Irish reunification. The Fine Gael leader's correspondence comes after his party last weekend published a "blueprint" for Irish unity at its Ard Fheis, with projections it could cost up to €25 billion a year. The party's proposals also include a new junior minister for North-South relations in a dedicated unit within the Department of An Taoiseach and the establishment of a dedicated sovereign wealth fund to deal with the potential costs of the transition. It all comes with a renewed focus on Irish unity in recent months following comments by US President Donald Trump during his Irish visit in September and with Fianna Fáil and Sinn Fein also pushing renewed proposals on how to achieve reunification. Mr Harris has contacted Fianna Fáil's Michael Martin, Sinn Féin 's Mary Lou McDonald, the Social Democrats' Cian O'Callaghan, the Labour Party's Ivana Bacik, Independent Ireland's Michael Collins, People Before Profit's Richard Boyd Barrett, Aontu's Peadar Toibin and the Green Party's Roderic O' Gorman seeking their views on Irish unity. He has also contacted leaders at Stormont, including the DUP's Gavin Robinson, the UUP's John Burrows, the TUV's Jim Allister, the SDLP's Claire Hanna and Naomi Long of the Alliance Party, asking for their views on Fine Gael's recent proposals.

stories.title: Baird mastering his craft after 'soul-sapping' injuries
stories.summary: This time last year, everything was coming together for Ryan Baird. The versatile forward had started the 2025/26 season for club and country in some of the best form of his career, and by the time Ireland took on South Africa at Aviva Stadium last November, Baird had firmly locked himself in as the first-choice blindside flanker following the retirement of Peter O'Mahony. Baird played every minute of Ireland's games against New Zealand, Japan and Australia that month, and was heading towards another 80-minute shift against the Springboks, before a fractured tibia ended his day, and ultimately wrecked his season. In the heat of the moment, he actually tried to continue, thinking it was just a severe dead leg, before the reality of the situation set in. "I started to play on, and then I went down. I was like, 'F**k, it's real sore'," he says. "The physio came on they strapped it up. Tadhg Beirne just goes – and you’re going to have to blur this one, ‘Get the f**k off the pitch if you can't run’ because I couldn't. I couldn't walk.

stories.title: EU seeks 'united voice' ahead of Ukraine peace talks
stories.summary: Events in Moscow gave the European Political Community (EPC) summit in Dublin a hard edge, shining a sharper spotlight than might have been expected on Micheál Martin's master of ceremonies role. Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelensky, on his third visit to Ireland in 12 months, has been trying to keep a grip on the Trump administration’s latest peace initiative, including two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, at which a European delegation turned up but was then sidelined by Russia. He also announced that Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite system was - once again - mysteriously downgraded, hindering Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian ballistic missile and jet-powered drone attacks. Then, unexpectedly, just before the EPC kicked off, it was announced that President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner would bounce from Abu Dhabi to the Kremlin and on to Baldonnel Aerodrome in Dublin (surely an itinerary first) to bring news of Vladimir Putin’s views on Europe’s potential involvement in the process. Having addressed the EPC plenary session at the Convention Centre and attended a Friends of Ukraine meeting on the margins, with UK prime minister Andy Burnham, President Zelensky then high-tailed it to a frigid aerodrome for talks with Mr Kushner and Mr Witkoff. Following an hour-long meeting, the three emerged to confirm that Europe would be invited to the next talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

stories.title: Euronext asks listed firms to phone after Outlook outage
stories.summary: European stock market operator Euronext has advised listed companies this morning to use the phone to communicate corporate information after an outage in Microsoft's Outlook email service. "Euronext Corporate Actions and Listing teams are currently experiencing an email communication disruption and are unable to receive emails," the company, which runs exchanges in Dublin, Paris, Brussels, Lisbon, Amsterdam, Oslo, Athens and Milan, said in a corporate filing. "For urgent matters relating to suspensions, corporate actions management, Oslo major shareholding notifications, MyEuronext or Newspoint, issuers and their agents are advised to contact the relevant Exchange Operator by telephone," it added. The company advised MyEuronext users to call through mobile phones and use two-factor authentication. Euronext did not say how it would guarantee safe identification of other callers. A spokesperson for the company did not immediately respond to a request for comment about that issue.

stories.title: Dept Q crew member dies after being injured at studio
stories.summary: A member of the crew for the Netflix series Dept Q has died after he was seriously injured at a film studio in Edinburgh. Producer Left Bank Pictures said it was "deeply shocked and saddened" by the man's death on Thursday. Emergency services were called to a report of a seriously injured man at FirstStage Studios in the Leith area of Edinburgh at around 3pm on Thursday. The man was pronounced dead at the scene a short time later, police said. A Police Scotland spokesman said: "The death is not being treated as suspicious. However, inquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances." FirstStage Studios has been home to multiple series for Netflix and Prime, according to its website, as well as the BAFTA-nominated film The Outrun.

stories.title: More than half of NI voters back UK rejoining EU - poll
stories.summary: More than half of voters in Northern Ireland believe the UK should rejoin the European Union a decade after the Brexit referendum, a new opinion poll has suggested. More than three-quarters of respondents to the new Queen's University Belfast poll also welcome the prospect of an upcoming EU-UK summit agreeing to reduce checks and controls on goods moving from Great Britain into Northern Ireland. The results of the latest public opinion polling, conducted for the university by LucidTalk, also indicate that support for the Windsor Framework continues to weaken, with 45% regarding it as "on balance a good thing for Northern Ireland," the lowest level since June 2021. Only 44% of respondents to the poll believe the Windsor Framework is an appropriate means of managing the effects of Brexit on the region, a decline from 60% in February 2024. The academics behind the poll said the findings highlight continuing divisions over the post-Brexit settlement and growing concerns about its economic, constitutional and political consequences. The Windsor Framework is the post-Brexit deal between the UK and the EU aimed at reducing trading frictions between Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

stories.title: Plans advanced for major upgrade of Limerick railway line
stories.summary: Iarnród Éireann has signed a contract with engineering firms Jacobs and AECOM to advance plans for a major upgrade of the railway between Limerick Colbert and Limerick Junction. The project will see preliminary designs developed and a planning application prepared for improvements along the approximately 34km route. The proposed works include 26km of double tracking, upgrades to signalling infrastructure, bridges and drainage, and improvements to level crossings. Iarnród Éireann said the additional infrastructure would allow more frequent services and improve journey times. The company is working towards submitting a planning application in 2027, with construction to follow. Increased services on the line are expected to begin operating from 2032.

stories.title: Mulhall Rock back with Tinahely after Rugby 7s tenure
stories.summary: After being away from the competitive arena for an extended period of time, former Ireland Women's 7s rugby captain Lucy Mulhall Rock has enjoyed being back out on a Gaelic football pitch with her native Tinahely in Wicklow this year. A key component of the seven-a-side game for the guts of 10 years, Mulhall Rock announced her international retirement in the aftermath of the Paris Olympics in 2024. While she did feature in group stage encounters with Great Britain and South Africa, a torn hamstring injury sustained in the latter game brought an abrupt halt to her on-field journey with Ireland in the French capital. This led to a prolonged stint on the sideline and even though she travelled with the Tinahely panel when they faced Kilmacud Crokes in a Leinster senior club football championship final 12 months ago, she was pregnant at this time with her son Fionn. However, Mulhall Rock subsequently returned to sporting action after giving birth earlier this year, and lined up alongside her sister Emily when Tinahely secured their 12th successive Wicklow senior crown with a final victory against Bray Emmets on 3 October. "I had our son just at the end of April. As did Sarah Hogan and Jessie Byrne, we were all within two weeks of each other. Then Jackie Kinch a couple of months later. All of us are back playing now. It has just been really enjoyable for me. I was always involved with the club to a degree, but when you’re in something like rugby, you were all in," Mulhall Rock acknowledged.

stories.title: 32 hospitalised after cruise ship capsizes in New Orleans
stories.summary: A tanker ship collided with a luxury paddle wheeler docked in New Orleans on the Mississippi River in the US yesterday, causing the cruise vessel to roll over and sink as passengers scurried to disembark and dozens were flung into the water. All aboard the stricken ship were accounted for after harbour personnel, firefighters and onlookers scrambled to pull fallen passengers to safety, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a press conference. Hailing the outcome as "a miracle on the Mississippi," she said 32 passengers from American ‌Cruise Lines paddle wheeler American Heritage ⁠were hospitalised, but "none with any type of critical injuries". Ms Moreno said roughly 180 to 190 passengers and crew members were aboard the American Heritage at the time of the incident. The cruise ship has a capacity for 150 passengers and was built in 2015, American Cruise Lines said on its website. The incident occurred about midday when the ‌tanker ship, the Atlantic Asphalt, "lost control and collided" with the docked cruise vessel, Ms Moreno said.

stories.title: Cunningham: Coleman 'hybrid role' a mistake
stories.summary: Former Republic of Ireland captain Kenny Cunningham says that Seamus Coleman's present 'hybrid role' is not sustainable and a decision needs to be made on his status within the set-up soon. The 38-year old Coleman is without a club after leaving Everton at the end of last season and once again has been excluded from the 24-man squad for this week's international window. However, unlike the previous four-game window, Coleman is around the camp this week, with Heimir Hallgrimsson explaining that the full-back would be involved in a hybrid capacity that will encompass training with the squad and a support role alongside the coaching staff. The Euro 2016 veteran, whose return to the starting line-up for the October and November games last year helped trigger a revival after the loss in Armenia, played the full 90 minutes and the opening period of extra-time in Ireland's agonising first round play-off shootout loss to Czechia in March. He recently said he "edging towards" retirement in a UK media appearance but so far has yet to make that call. "After that game at the Czech Republic, we all knew it was going to be two and a half years down the road until the next major finals at the European Championships.

stories.title: Starship reaches orbit ahead of return, booster explodes
stories.summary: SpaceX launched the 15th flight of its Starship spacecraft from Texas in the US yesterday, on a mission the company hopes will be the first round-trip voyage into orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth. Plans call for Starship's uncrewed upper-stage vessel to re-enter the atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and return to its launch tower today for an engine-controlled touchdown assisted by a catch-landing mechanism. SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and "chopstick" arm technology to recover the Starship's lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within minutes of the launch. However, the booster, for reasons not immediately clear, was diverted from its return flight path to the Gulf of Mexico and momentarily hovered aloft before exploding a short distance over the sea surface. SpaceX mission controllers hope they will be able to steer Starship's upper stage back to home base at the end of its flight. Bringing the top portion of the spacecraft back intact would mark a breakthrough in the ambitions of Elon Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, to reduce spaceflight costs by developing a fully recyclable rocket system.

stories.title: Postcard from Linz: City with growing football footprint
stories.summary: If there was any indication that Linz was bit of an afterthought outside of Austria's borders, a couple of anecdotal tales of Irish fans making early bookings for Vienna summed it up. The Republic of Ireland were drawn into the same UEFA Nations League group as Austria all the way back in February. stories.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in China next week
stories.summary: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen in China next week, the White House has announced. Mr Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up the war in Iran. However, he is not expected to discuss Russia's war with Ukraine, US officials said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. "The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," Ms Wales said. One of the major conflicts dominating Mr Trump's second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.

stories.title: AI should be for the benefit of mankind - Taoiseach
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence should be designed for the benefit rather than the "ruination of mankind", Taoiseach Micheál Martin has said. EU leaders discussed the future of AI during an informal meeting in Dublin today. British-Canadian computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton gave the heads of state a "stark message" on the potential of AI to destroy the world. Professor Hinton, the Nobel Prize-winning 'godfather of AI', and Arthur Mensch, chief executive of AI start-up Mistral, joined leaders for the summit. The Taoiseach said Professor Hinton was advocating strongly for global governance and global regulation of AI. "He made it very clear, he's a scientist, not a policy expert, but he was clear that Europe was the bastion of regulation in relation to AI. It's very important," Mr Martin said this evening.

stories.title: Mother facing eviction denied respite for non-verbal sons
stories.summary: A Dublin mother who is being evicted from her home with her two severely autistic teenage sons has said the Health Service Executive (HSE) has repeatedly told her that emergency residential care is unavailable. It comes despite Government assurances made last week that emergency placements for people with disabilities would be funded. Yvonne Nolan, her two 16-year-old sons who are severely autistic and non-verbal, and her daughter are facing eviction from their home in Dublin next Tuesday. The boys have severe and complex needs, and their home has been specifically adapted to keep them safe. "I've like bulletproof, shatterproof windows upstairs. The electrics, the locks: you'll see where you're going and you won't be able to get out. "Everything has to be secured to keep them safe based on their needs," she said.

stories.title: Gardaí want to speak to couple after body found in Dublin
stories.summary: Investigators are seeking to speak to a couple following the discovery of a man's body in suspicious circumstances in Dublin. The man's body was found in the Phoenix Park near the Wellington Monument at about 10.20am. The man's body has been removed from the scene, which was preserved for technical examination. Gardaí believe the man could have been homeless and may have been sleeping rough. It is understood the man has some suspicious injuries on his body, which gardaí say may be knife wounds. However, they said the results of the post-mortem examination will determine the course of the investigation and they do not yet know how these injuries occurred.

stories.title: Finland take narrow lead to Cork after Tampere snowstorm
stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland have work to do if they're to make next year's European U21 Championships after falling to a 1-0 defeat against Finland. The match was highly disrupted by heavy snow in Tampere, with the teams taken off the pitch in the first half, so that lines could be cleared, and the start of the second half delayed by nearly an hour. Onni Helen got the only goal in first half stoppage time and the Finns will feel they were unlucky not to have scored more, having hit the upright on a number of occasions. But Jim Crawford's side did begin to battle and Jamie Mullins also hit the crossbar with a header, while Owen Elding had a massive chance to equalise cleared off the line. They couldn't force home a goal but things are still finally poised ahead the return leg in Cork on Tuesday. Ireland had only reached the play-off by the skin of their teeth, finishing their group D campaign with four wins on the spin to scrape through at Slovakia's expense.

stories.title: Research report calls for revamp of youth GAA competition
stories.summary: A new research report has called for increased focus to be placed on the future design and organisation of youth GAA competitions. The paper, 'Shaping the future of juvenile Gaelic Games – evidence to inform a youth games framework' states at the outset that it does not seek to remove competition from juvenile GAA and that proposed modified games would still retain score, challenge and competitive identity. The recommendations are intended to inform future consideration of youth games policy rather than announce changes to existing competition structures. The report advocates further consultation, piloting and evaluation of proposed approaches before any wider implementation. But the document has heralded a call to ensure that competition serves development, participation, belonging, and long-term retention — rather than leaving behind those who need support most. The paper, written by Dr Michael McKay, Dr Paul Donnelly, Dr Richard Bowles and Dr Peter Horgan, recommends that the GAA should introduce a national, evidence-informed Youth Games Framework for U13–U17 players.

In its correction, Sky News acknowledged that the comments may have misled viewers about members of the band. It said a contributor had made remarks about Kneecap and the alleged use of SLAPPs, adding that "the remarks were unfounded". stories.title: Tinder owner fined €11m by Data Protection Commission
stories.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission has issued an €11m fine on Tinder's parent company Match for failing to comply with GDPR rules. The fine is in relation to a tool that allows users to request their personal data. Data Commissioner Niamh Sweeney said the fine was issued because Tinder's tool only gave users a portion of the data it held on them. "What you would get is the number of times you swiped left or right on a particular day, the time you logged in, or the number of matches you made in a day", she said. "But there are other types of data, analytics data that wouldn't have been included, that could include your gender, your latitude or longitude, the city you were logging in from, and other types of data", she said. Match has already indicated that it will appeal the fine, meaning the payment will have to wait for a decision from the European Court of Justice.

stories.title: Pochettino confirmed as new Manchester United manager
stories.summary: Manchester United have reached an agreement for Mauricio Pochettino to become their new head coach. The Red Devils have agreed a deal which releases the Argentinian and his coaching staff from their duties with the United States national team after their two matches against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday. Pochettino succeeds Michael Carrick, who was sacked by United on Thursday after their worst start to a campaign since 1986. Pochettino, who led the US to the last 16 of the World Cup on home soil earlier this year, has previously managed in the Premier League with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. Pochettino is understood to have signed a two-and-a-half-year deal with United, taking him through to the summer of 2029. His appointment has the unanimous endorsement of club leadership and the ownership and Pochettino was the only coach the club spoke to directly as a potential successor to Carrick.
